newsitem.title: FRANCE: 2,000 French volunteers to drive party-goers home.
newsitem.headline: 2,000 French volunteers to drive party-goers home.

text.p: French party-goers who drink too much at New Year can get driven home free in a road safety scheme comprising 2,000 volunteer chauffeurs that has snowballed since it was set up six years ago.

The so-called Saint-Bernard operation, inspired from a Canadian idea, will help revellers get home between midnight and 8 a.m. on Wednesday (2300 and 0700 GMT)-- one of the most dangerous times of the year on French roads.
"Too much to drink at New Year. A bit tired? Don't hesitate...Contact the Saint-Bernards," the group, organised by the Red Cross and car magazine Autoplus, says in a nationwide telephone hotline.

Launched in the eastern city of Strasbourg in 1990, the project counts 2,000 volunteers with 400 cars, with the Paris region benefiting for a first time. Last year, there were 1,500 volunteers and 220 cars, up from 200 volunteers with 50 cars in 1994.
When called out, teams of three volunteers come to pick up revellers. One of them drives the party-goer's car, the second sits in the back with the car owner, and the third drives an escort car.
